hero.headline: Dodonai vs Clio: Purpose-Built Legal AI, Alongside Your Practice Management
hero.subheadline: Clio is where you run your firm — matters, billing, intake. Its assistant, Clio Duo, adds AI on top. But the heavy document work — deposition summaries, medical-record chronologies, custom workflows — needs AI built for it. Here's where Dodonai fits, and how it works alongside Clio, not instead of it.

sections.heading: What Clio Does — and Where a Different Tool Earns Its Keep
paragraphs: Clio is the practice-management backbone for tens of thousands of firms: matter management, time tracking, billing, client intake, and calendaring in one place. Clio Duo layers a general AI assistant on top — it can summarize a matter, surface information, and help draft routine messages inside the platform.

That's a genuinely useful assistant for running the practice. It is not, however, purpose-built for the document-heavy legal work: turning a 200-page deposition into a page-line summary with accurate citations, building a medical-record chronology from thousands of pages, or running a custom workflow tuned to how your firm actually works. For that, firms reach for AI designed specifically for the job.
This isn't a question of replacing Clio. It's a question of what handles the document work your matter-management system was never built to do.

sections.heading: Clio + Dodonai, Together
paragraphs: The strongest setup for most firms isn't one tool or the other. It's Clio running the practice — matters, billing, deadlines — with Dodonai handling the AI-heavy document work and any custom automation your team needs. You get the system of record you already trust and purpose-built AI for the work that actually eats your associates' hours.

If you're weighing whether Clio Duo is enough for your deposition and medical-record work, the honest answer is: it's a solid assistant for the platform, and Dodonai is built for the documents. Try both against a real file and see the difference for yourself.

faq.question: Does Dodonai replace Clio?
faq.answer: No. Clio is your practice-management system — matters, billing, intake. Dodonai is purpose-built AI for the document-heavy work (deposition summaries, medical-record chronologies) and custom AI agents. Most firms run both: Clio for the practice, Dodonai for the AI layer around it.

faq.question: Is Clio Duo enough for deposition or medical-record summaries?
faq.answer: Clio Duo is a general assistant built into the platform — useful for summarizing matters and drafting routine messages. It isn't purpose-built for producing page-line deposition summaries with reliable citations or medical-record chronologies from thousands of pages. That's what Dodonai is designed for.

faq.question: Can Dodonai work alongside Clio?
faq.answer: Yes. Dodonai is designed to run around the tools you already use rather than replace them. You keep Clio as your system of record and use Dodonai for the AI document work and any custom workflows.

faq.question: Is my client data secure with Dodonai?
faq.answer: Privileged files need SOC 2, HIPAA, and encryption at minimum. Dodonai is SOC 2 certified, HIPAA compliant, and AES-256 encrypted, with BAAs on every account. Your files are never used to train AI, and you control when they're deleted.

faq.question: What does 'you own the code' mean?
faq.answer: For custom AI agents our {{link:/ai-managed-services/|managed-services team}} builds for your firm, the resulting workflows are yours — you're not locked into leasing access forever. It's a different model from standard SaaS.
